newsitem.title: UK: S&P AFFIRMS SUNDERLAND MARINE CLAIMS RATING.
newsitem.headline: S&P AFFIRMS SUNDERLAND MARINE CLAIMS RATING.

text.p: LONDON , May 1 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its triple-B' claims-paying ability rating of Sunderland Marine Mutual Insurance Company Limited (SMMI).

The rating is based on SMMI's strong niche position both domestically and internationally, stable client base, good operating performance and adequate capitalization. Offsetting factors include high dependence on reinsurers, limited financial flexibility and reliance on an industry sector that is under increasing economic and political pressure.

-- SMMI enjoys a strong position in its niche markets of insuring fishing vessels (and associated protection and indemnity P&I risks) and aquaculture business. The fishing industry has come under pressure from an increasingly stringent economic and political environment. However, SMMI has partially addressed this risk by diversifying into aquaculture insurance and new geographic areas, also resulting in a wider spread of risk.
-- Excellent continuity of the customer base with renewals on U.K. business approaching 100% in 1996. This is achieved through a dedicated approach to customer service and strong local knowledge.

-- Good operating performance that has been maintained for a number of years in a way that is consistent with the company's mutual status. SMMI benefits from greater stability in both its claims experience and premium income, compared to other marine insurers, due to a combination of strict underwriting discipline and the niche nature of the business. This is borne out by the combined ratio which has remained below 101% over the last four years, averaging 97% over this period. Return on revenue was a moderate 5% in 1996 and is held back by relatively low investment returns, resulting from modest, albeit adequate, reserving levels.

-- Adequate capitalization. The company has fundamentally moved away from relying on supplementary calls to support underwriting operations and by the end of 1996 had built up its free reserves to UK22 million (US$38 million). This represented, according to Standard & Poor's risk based capital model, a 1.1 times coverage of the amount required to support current activities, which is consistent with the 5 year average. The free reserves are protected by a comprehensive reinsurance program, which may ultimately leave the company exposed to the quality of its reinsurance.
-- SMMI's relatively small size and mutual status limit its financial flexibility. However, we expect additional funding requirements to remain minimal over the near to medium term.

-- Management's strict underwriting guidelines will not be relaxed in the pursuit of new business growth, which is expected to principally derive from aquaculture risks, for which the company is already a leading world carrier.
-- Free reserves will continue to grow, principally through investment income, and be maintained at a satisfactory level over the near term.
-- Adverse economic and political developments in the fishing industry will not impact current levels of business in the near to medium term, Standard & Poor's said.
